image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Six-storey narrow Thai student dormitory building, tall deep block faced in small beige ceramic tiles with a grid of square windows behind ornate steel security grilles, a stack of small square balconies up the centre of the front with air-conditioning condensers and drying clothes, a large red-and-white sign on the front parapet reading dormitory, ground floor split into a coin laundry shop and a minimart with roller shutters and a tiled entrance stair, deep plain side walls with rows of small bathroom vents, flat roof with a steel water tank tower Materials: beige glazed mosaic tile with dark grout and grime under every window, oxidised black-painted steel grilles, cream painted side render with damp staining, galvanised steel roller shutters, rust-streaked steel water tank on an angle-iron frame.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.90: silhouette 0.95 on a band table at 0.0055 / 0.0069 of height with both residuals traced to percentile bands at the parapet and the ground-floor paving; structure 0.92 with every identity feature present at the plate's count and the proxy's position; form 0.88, material 0.86 and lighting 0.86 held down by the lifted dark tones, generic garments and the invented rear and -X elevations. 5,848/32,000 triangles, 15/24 draw calls, 14/16 materials, 15/32 unique geometries.

featureReviews.evidence: Four window columns at the proxy's +Z depth-map positions (x -5.40 / -2.77 / +2.77 / +5.40, rectangles 51-123 / 164-234 / 399-471 / 511-584 px at 42.66 px/m) either side of a 1.9 m balcony column on five floors at a 3.0 m pitch (recess tops 249/377/507/634/762 px); five dark bands 0.30 m tall across the full width, each projecting 0.44 m under the balcony box above it; mosaic tile as a 50 mm multiplier canvas with grime streaks under all twenty sills. Band table: mean |delta width| 0.0055 of height.
featureReviews.notes: Bands authored #665744 (luma 91, sat 0.33) over the plate's #464137 and the grille glass #274D3E (sat 0.49) over #312F2A so the segmenter holds them on chroma; the first grille canvas at luma 120 read as a pale green screen and was darkened. The sill streaks were doubled in strength after the first render showed them as faint.

featureReviews.evidence: Five balconies as real 1.2 m recesses -- holes through the 0.30 m facade extrusion with liner cheeks, a ceiling and a floor plug behind, the body core's front face as the back wall -- under tiled parapet boxes 2.15 x 1.15 m standing 0.45 m proud (proxy front_x: front blobs 20 px = 0.47 m); a condenser high-left in every recess, three shirts on a rail in two, two towels over the fourth-floor parapet. Turntable gate passes at every azimuth (0.20-0.51 percent enclosed background, all of it lattice gaps).
featureReviews.notes: The recess walls are authored #64503A (luma 84, sat 0.42) against the plate's #24231D shadow; the first tone (#76644F) read as tan rather than shadow and was darkened while keeping the chroma the gate needs. The balcony floor is hidden inside the parapet box -- an exterior shell, nothing behind it.

featureReviews.evidence: A 1.58 m tiled parapet band (18.42..20.0) carrying a 5.5 x 1.25 m DORMITORY board over the top windows; a four-leg lattice tower centred (4.6, -3.6) from the proxy occupancy rows (x 0.71..0.91 W, z 0.07..0.18 H), 3.0 m base tapering to 2.1 m at 22.0 with a ring and crossed braces on every face of three tiers, a railed 2.5 m platform, a ladder, and a 0.88 m ribbed tank to 24.0; a grey deck inside a 0.30 m parapet.
featureReviews.notes: The lattice's open gaps are the whole of the gate's enclosed background; legs were widened 0.12 -> 0.14 and braces 0.06 -> 0.08 and the gate holds at 0.44 / 0.51 percent at 0 / 270 without --allow-holes. Steel authored #684838 (sat 0.46) -- the first #7A5440 rendered orange against the plate's dark rust.

featureReviews.evidence: A 0.48 m tiled fascia 0.45 m proud at 3.3 (proxy px 866-877); two 2.6 m shutter leaves left of a 1.9 m stair entrance recessed 2.0 m (proxy row 900: 144 at px 286-355), one shutter and a dark-framed glazed unit with a door right of it; six 0.16 m steps rising to a door panel.
featureReviews.notes: Shutter slat valleys were first drawn at a 0.45 multiplier and the 0 frame read them as backdrop (5,100 of 8,400 flagged pixels); they ship at 0.70 on a #96968F base. The stair moved from the grey deck material to the cream paint after the render showed it grey against the plate's white tiles.

featureReviews.evidence: Cream #DAD2C0 flank with a grid of recessed panel grooves (verticals at 0.9 / 4.9 / 9.3 m from the front, horizontals at the band levels) as a 1024^2 multiplier canvas on rear-to-front UVs, a condenser pair per floor at z -0.95 / -0.20 (proxy +X map rows at z px 211-230 / 284-305) with drip stains under each, rain streaks off the parapet and grime at the base.
featureReviews.notes: The -X flank mirrors +X and the rear is plain cream, both unobserved and recorded at 0.55-0.60. The condenser fan discs at a 0.34 tint were read as backdrop in the 270 frame; they ship at 0.50.

featureReviews.evidence: Fourteen materials, all measured off the plate at PBR confidence 0.730-0.860: #DCC9A8 tile over #D4C4AD clean samples, #665744 bands, #DAD2C0 paint, #96968F shutters, #684838 rust steel, #8A847A galvanised tank; seven seeded canvases carry the mosaic, grooves, grille, slats, rust, streaks and board.
featureReviews.notes: Every dark tone is lifted from its plate measurement and held on chroma; each lift and its measurement is recorded on the material. Nothing synthesises the five-canvas procedural set.

name: Student Dormitory Block
notes: The university-district hor phak, the fourth of four six-storey residential shells. Exterior shell only, no interior geometry: the shop units are roller shutters and a tinted near-opaque shopfront pane, the balconies are a single central column of real recesses with tiled parapet boxes standing 0.45 m proud, the window grilles are a canvas graphic (not modelled bars), and the mosaic tile facade is a seamless canvas tile. The plain cream side walls carry recessed panel grooves and a pair of condensers per floor; a level builder places them against neighbours. The sign is generic Thai signage, not a trademark. Sizing CORRECTED 2026-08-27 from the list-time 12 x 19.5 x 24 (a shophouse-width deep-plot guess) on the Meshy v7 proxy of the plate, which normalises to w:h:d = 0.620 : 1 : 0.555 with the rooftop tank tower on top and the body top at 0.82 H: anchoring the proxy floor pitch of 128 px (534.6 px per proxy unit) at 3.0 m gives 42.66 px/m, a 613 px body = 14.4 m wide (four 3.07 m room bays either side of a 2.1 m balcony column), a 12.8 m deep body (front_x map 545 px) plus 0.45 m balcony/fascia projection = 13.3, a 20.0 m parapet top (854 px), a 3.4 m shop ground floor and a tank tower to 24.0 m; condensers add 0.25 m per flank (14.9). The plate itself shows the front WIDER than the side, not a deep plot. Balconies, recess walls and grille shadows must be authored above the turntable backdrop luma of 58 or the silhouette gate reads them as holes.
